references.text: Abraham also laughed at the thought of having children in his old age, which mirrors Sarah's reaction of laughter and disbelief.
Sarah says that God has made her laugh, and all who hear about it will laugh with her—a return to the laughter when she heard the promise.
Sarah is mentioned for her faith in God's promise of a son despite her advanced age, showing how doubt was transformed into faith.
Paul uses Abraham as an example of faith: he hoped against all hope and knew that his and Sarah's bodies were past childbearing age, yet still trusted in God's promise.
Peter refers to Sarah calling Abraham "lord," which directly reflects Sarah's words "and my lord is old" in this verse.
